newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian share trade slumps amid closure.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian share trade slumps amid closure.

text.p: The number of shares traded on the Palestine Securities Exchange plunged to an all-time low on Sunday in what the exchange said reflected the impact of an Israeli security clampdown on Palestinian areas.
Only 4,431 shares worth 14,953 Jordanian dinars changed hands, compared with 140,379 shares worth 226,368 dinars on Wednesday. Stocks in only six of 16 quoted companies were traded.
The Jerusalem index closed at 105.05, up from 104.63 on Wednesday. The exchange holds two sessions a week.

"There's total disinterest in securities under conditions of the closure," said PSE general manager Safwan Bataina. "People find that under such daily suffering, trading securities is about the last thing on their list of priorities," he said.
"I expect more of the same as long as these measures are enforced," he added.
Israel closed its borders to thousands of Palestinian workers after a double suicide bombing by Islamic militants in a Jewish market in Jerusalem on July 30.
Israel also restricted travel between Palestinian cities, villages and towns on the West Bank.
Though Israel has eased some of the internal restrictions, the town of Ramallah where the exchange is located remains under special Israeli security measures.
Bataina said he had implemented a remote trading system so brokers unable to reach the exchange could continue to work.

Shares in the Palestine Telecommunication company rose 1.31 percent to 1.55 dinars per share. Shares in the Jerusalem Cigarette Company, in its second week on the exchange, closed at 4.96 dinars, up from 4.95 on Wednesday.

The Palestine Real Estate Investment Company closed down 1.96 percent at one dinar per share while shares in the Palestine Development and Investment Company fell two percent to 696.7 dinars. The two other stocks traded were unchanged.
Trading is conducted in dinars or dollars in the absence of a Palestinian currency.
